title: Cartella Ops safeguard handoff and rollback rehearsal
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-05-03
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha, Marc, Dina (Redwood) — Liam, Priya, Daniel (Cartella)

Summary:
Quick follow-up after the weekend degradation incident. Goal was to walk through the new ops safeguard runbook, confirm rollback and canary rehearshal steps, and agree next actions for security signoff and a dry-run. Discussed KV/cache warmup, autoscale thresholds, and SSO audit links.

Topics:
- Incident recap and root hypothesis
- Runbook walkthrough (safeguard, rollback)
- Access & audit requirements (KMS, SSO, SAML)
- Scheduled dry-run and benchmark windows
- Commercial ask: pilot concession and dedicated capacity timeline

Action items (short):
- See action items section below for owners/due dates.

Transcript body: 
[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to do a short handoff from last weekend's outage, run the updated ops safeguard, and rehearse the rollback. Liam, Priya, did you have any immediate blockers before we start?
[00:18] Liam: No, thanks. I mostly want to understand the trigger thresholds — why autoscale didn't pick up the spike fast enough; also the retros had some questions about KV cache heat.
[00:30] Marc: Right, the spike was an unusual seq len distribution paired with large prefix reuse. Our runtime's continuous batching backlogged because the cache entries were being evicted — so the first few requests hit cold path and amplified latency.
[00:45] Priya: When you say cache entries evicted, do you mean the KV cache on the inference side or some application cache? We saw keys drop on our side as well.
[00:56] Marc: Great question — mostly the model-side KV cache. There's a small memory pressure event that coincided with a big burst; eviction policy kicked in. There was also an incident where our autoscaler mis-inferred pod readiness because a liveness probe was flapping under the CPU burst.
[01:15] Daniel: Can you remind me of the probe config? We saw a pretty aggressive 5s timeout in the screenshot.
[01:22] Marc: Yeah, earlier config was 5s. We've updated suggestions to 15s for heavy tokenization workloads and to use readiness gating based on the runtime health endpoint rather than CPU. But that change went out during the mitigation step, so we couldn't benefit retroactively.
[01:36] Aisha: That's important — the runbook now includes a preflight check for readiness gating and a staged probe adjustment. We'll talk through that.
[01:44] Marc: Walkthrough slide one — guardrail overview. Step 1: detect anomaly using latency and token exit percentiles. Step 2: evaluate fallback policy — try warmup cache + soft-throttle. Step 3: escalate to rollback to previous model/profile if warmup fails for N minutes.
[02:04] Priya: The warmup step — is that automatic, or do you expect runbook operator to hit an endpoint to populate prefixes?
[02:11] Marc: We support both. There's an automated warmup route that uses the most frequent prompt prefixes observed historically, but for customer-specific flows, we recommend a targeted warmup via the runbook where SRE triggers a controlled ramp using the /internal/warmup endpoint. The caveat: the warmup traffic still counts toward your quota in hosted mode unless you're on Dedicated.
[02:33] Liam: That quota part is a concern for us — we consumed a ton of tokens last month just on baseline tests. If we do frequent dry-runs, costs will balloon.
[02:41] Aisha: Understood. We proposed a pilot concession for the dry-run windows — we'll include that in the next steps.
[02:48] Daniel: On security: the runbook currently references KMS rotation and audit logs. We need the exact retention for logs to satisfy our compliance team.
[02:57] Dina: Audit logs are configurable; hosted defaults to 90 days but we can enable long-term export to your S3 bucket. The Private deployment offers longer retention with HSM-backed KMS if you need it.
[03:12] Daniel: Export is fine, but can we avoid plaintext keys landing in logs? The previous export included a token stub which our DLP flagged.
[03:21] Marc: Right — token redaction is set to mask 12 chars by default but we will add an extra layer to ensure no plaintext API keys are present. We'll push a config that strips full tokens from exported payloads.
[03:33] Priya: Great. On the rehearsal, can we step through a rollback? Real-world step-by-step, including the routing fallback to the cheaper model variant?
[03:42] Marc: Sure — I'll narrate and Priya can play operator. Step A: detection fires, the safeguard runner attempts a cache refresh. Step B: if latency doesn't drop under threshold in 120s, the runner toggles traffic weighting to the canary variant or a model with smaller context window, depending on policy. Step C: if that fails, full rollback replaces the model binary with the last known-good version and restarts the runtime with staged ramp.
[04:06] Priya: If we do a full rollback, do we need to coordinate with our config mgmt to adjust client SDKs? We had a problem previously with client pinning to a variant.
[04:18] Marc: Good catch — clients should not be hard-pinned to a single variant. Our recommended approach: client tolerance with graceful fallback in SDK. We'll share code sample that checks model variant compatibility and accepts 3xx-style redirect if necessary.
[04:33] Liam: We had one more issue — the regional fallback went to a region with different privacy controls, which triggered a compliance alert. Can we add region-aware fallback rules?
[04:43] Aisha: Yes — the routing policy now supports region tags and will avoid fallbacks to disallowed regions. We'll include routing rules in the runbook and surface them in the Console under route policies.
[04:55] Daniel: Speaking of Console, can we get a trace that ties an API key to the rollout event? We need auditability for the rollback action.
[05:03] Dina: The Console event stream already tags rollout events with operator identity (SSO). We'll add a cross-link to the request IDs and add an export that joins timeline + request snapshots for forensics.
[05:17] Marc: Quick demo now — I'm going to trigger a simulated detection in the sandbox so we can watch the safeguard runner. Priya, ready?
[05:24] Priya: Ready.
[05:28] [demo noise — a pause while Marc triggers the sandbox event] 
[05:40] Marc: You should see a spike in the Console alert view; runner is executing warmup. Warmup traffic shows prefix population but latencies still above threshold. Now the runner is shifting 20% traffic to the canary variant.
[05:55] Priya: I see 20% weight shift. Latency dropping slightly. Okay, increment to 50% manually?
[06:03] Marc: Done. Note that we emit an audit event on each weight change.
[06:09] Liam: The audit event contains a user hash, but not the full email — is that configurable?
[06:15] Dina: We mask email by default but we can enable full identity for enterprise accounts under contract with an additional audit retention add-on.
[06:26] Priya: Shrug, we probably want full identity for postmortem windows. We'll coordinate with legal.
[06:33] Marc: While that's moving, two other technical notes: 1) We recommend setting CPU headroom and request queue thresholds more conservatively for your traffic pattern. 2) We've added a tuning knob to the runtime that delays KV eviction under burst conditions by a configurable grace window.
[06:50] Liam: How does that grace window interact with memory overall? Could we cause OOMs?
[06:56] Marc: It's bounded. The grace window trades short-term memory with transient latency; the runner monitors mem pressure and will lower grace if the system approaches OOM, plus we have a soft OOM killer that prioritizes background batchers.
[07:12] Daniel: For our security signoff, we need the runbook text block that describes who is authorized to initiate a rollback and the exact SSO group required.
[07:21] Aisha: We'll add a required SSO group tag to the runbook JSON and make that part of the gating check — only identities in the 'Cartella-Infra-Operators' group can finalize rollbacks.
[07:33] Priya: Perfect. Also we need a communication play: Slack channel, priority email, and incident bridge recording. Can you automate that from the runner?
[07:42] Dina: Yes — runner can post to your incident webhook; we can provide a Terraform example for the webhook and Slack-channel mapping.
[07:52] Liam: About the dry-run: we want to schedule a non-business-hour window next Thursday where Redwood will run two rehearsals and Cartella will observe.
[07:59] Aisha: Proposed window is Thursday 02:00–04:00 PT. We can run a warmup, a 50% canary shift, and full rollback rehearsal. That will be the pilot dry-run.
[08:12] Priya: Token usage again — we need the pilot concession so the dry-run doesn't hit our monthly quota.
[08:18] Aisha: We'll include a credit for the rehearsal hours and discount on token billing for the pilot period; agreed?
[08:24] Liam: Sounds good, pending procurement signoff.
[08:28] Daniel: Minor note: during the last incident, parts of the trace showed 'KV cache miss' as 'K-V cass mish' in the logs — the transcription or instrumentation had corruption. Can you make the log names stable?
[08:40] Marc: We'll normalize naming and add a versioned schema for log keys so parsers don't break.
[08:47] [crosstalk] 
[08:53] Aisha: Let's capture the decisions: runbook update accepted, scheduled dry-run 2028-05-10 02:00–04:00 PT, Redwood to provide concession credit, Redwood to push token redaction and log normalization changes, and provide the updated runbook with SSO gating.
[09:14] Priya: Can we also do a short tabletop with the compliance team before the dry-run? One hour to verify exports and retention.
[09:22] Dina: Yes — we'll set up a compliance tabletop on 2028-05-06.
[09:27] Liam: On metrics, can you add a post-run dashboard that shows warmup effectiveness — e.g., prefix hit rate and latency tail before/after?
[09:36] Marc: We'll add a dashboard tile and share a short how-to doc for interpreting it.
[09:43] Aisha: Anything else from Cartella?
[09:46] Priya: One last thing — if we move to Dedicated next quarter, what's the migration window and expected downtime?
[09:54] Marc: Typical plan is a phased migration with zero downtime if clients use model indirection. If clients are pinned, we include a brief maintenance window. We'll share a migration playbook and ETA of 4–6 weeks once contracts are signed.
[10:08] Liam: Okay thanks.
[10:11] Aisha: Great — we'll capture next steps. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
next_steps: 2028-05-06: Compliance tabletop with Redwood (Dina to schedule)
Aisha to send pilot concession details and credit schedule
Marc to push token redaction + log key normalization config
Marc to share migration playbook for Dedicated and client indirection sample code
action_items: Aisha Khan - Send runbook + escalation playbook and pilot concession terms (Due 2028-05-05)
Dina Morales - Schedule compliance tabletop with Cartella (Due 2028-05-04)
Marc Hsu - Implement token redaction config and log key normalization, share PR link (Due 2028-05-07)
Priya Rao - Validate SSO group membership list and provide Cartella operator emails (Due 2028-05-04)
Liam O'Neal - Confirm procurement signoff and token credit acceptance (Due 2028-05-08)
